correctness.rationale: Derivations have quotient block A, central eigenvalue tr A and a free row v; automorphisms have quotient B and central multiplier det B. The shear changes the row by -w adj(A), bijective if D is periodic. Thus full conjugacy reduces to rational similarity, with q² copies of each matrix in a class. Since T⁶-1 is separable, the exact-order filter applies to semisimple blocks with a,b,a+b in μ6. The displayed resultant can be checked without a computer: factor F=(T²-1)(T²-T+1), use G(1)=21 and G(-1)=-1, and reduce G mod T²-T+1 to 14(T-1), with root-product of (T-1) equal to 1. The resultant is -4116. For p≠7 the allowed unordered pairs are the pairs in each of the two cosets of μ3; Frobenius fixes all six for q≡1 and just the inverse pair in each coset for q≡5 mod 6. If both eigenvalues are cube roots their sum has cube -1. No possible sum of two signs is a sign in these characteristics. In p=7, choose distinct nonopposite pairs, 15-3=12, and include six scalar blocks. The sum of two different elements of {1,2,4} is never in that set, while doubling keeps it invariant, giving exactly the three scalar order-three classes and three scalar order-six classes. Centralizer orders give the table including extension fields. The uploaded code was inspected, not executed; it enumerates prime-field quotient blocks, and printed orbit histogram keys are quotient-class sizes (multiply by q² for full derivations).
